In 1920, one year after the Treaty of Versailles, a little-documented planner proposed erasing every border in Central Europe and replacing them with dozens of wedge-shaped 'cantons' radiating from a single capital.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ P.A. Maas called it "The New Europe With Lasting Peace." His logic: nationalism and disputed borders had just caused a war that killed millions, so the fix was to stop drawing borders around nations at all.

2/ The plan folds Germany, the former Austria-Hungary, Poland, and chunks of France, Italy and Ukraine into a single union. Berlin, Warsaw, Munich, Marseille, Milan and Odessa all appear as canton capitals — spokes on one giant wheel.

3/ At the hub sits the "Saint Stephen-Vienna Union," the seat of government for the whole federation — a deliberate nod to the old Habsburg lands, redesigned as a neutral center of gravity instead of a national one.

4/ Maas's plan never had any chance of adoption. The Paris Peace Conference had just spent a year drawing new nation-states out of Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire — the opposite instinct: sovereignty for ethnic groups, not dissolving them into cantons.

5/ It fits a pattern of the era: 1920 also saw the League of Nations open in Geneva, part of a wave of pacifists, engineers and dreamers all sketching blueprints to make war structurally impossible. Almost none survive as more than curiosities today.

6/ A century later, this odd wheel-shaped Europe is a reminder of how many people looked at the ruins of WWI and concluded the nation-state itself was the problem.
